'''Lillian Christie McDermott''' (1931 – July 8, 2020) was an American physicist. In the early 1970s, McDermott established the Physics Education Group (PEG) at the [[University of Washington]] to "improve the teaching and learning of physics from kindergarten all the way through graduate school." She was recognized for her many contributions to the field of [[physics education research]] with an election to the [[American Physical Society]] in 1990.

==Early life and education==
McDermott was born in 1931 and raised in [[Washington Heights, Manhattan]] to Greek immigrant parents. Her father was a lawyer in the Greek government prior to immigrating and her mother came to the United States as a teenager. She graduated from [[Hunter College High School]], at the time an all-girls school, before enrolling at [[Vassar College]] for her [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree.<ref name="Zierler2">{{cite web |last1=Zierler |first1=David |date=April 19, 2020 |title=Oral History Interviews: Lillian McDermott |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/44460 |access-date=April 28, 2021 |website=aip.org}}</ref>

While a student at Vassar College, McDermott had a music scholarship that funded her piano lessons, and she took courses in music theory, art history, and philosophy.<ref name="science2">{{cite web |date=2015 |title=The science of teaching science |url=https://www.washington.edu/facultystaff/lecture/2015-university-faculty-lecture/ |access-date=April 28, 2021 |website=washington.edu}}</ref> She also studied physics and received a bachelor's degree in physics in 1952.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Lillian Christie McDermott - Obituary |url=https://www.aapt.org/aboutaapt/Lillian_McDermott_obit.cfm |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=www.aapt.org}}</ref><ref name="Zierler2" /> Following this, she enrolled at [[Columbia University]] for her graduate degree in physics with a specialization in nuclear physics.<ref name="Zierler2" /><ref name=":0" /> She received her PhD in 1959.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Centennial News: Education Session |url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/199901/centennial-education.cfm |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Upon completing her formal education, McDermott began teaching physics full time at City College before moving to the [[University of Washington]] (UW) with her husband for a post-doctoral position.<ref name="Zierler">{{cite web |last1=Zierler |first1=David |date=April 19, 2020 |title=Oral History Interviews: Lillian McDermott |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/44460 |access-date=April 28, 2021 |website=aip.org}}</ref>

Although her husband was granted a faculty position, she was unable to join him due to anti-nepotism rules. She sought employment at [[Seattle University]] before the rules were struck down and she joined the Department of Physics at UW.<ref name="obit">{{cite web |title=Lillian Christie McDermott |url=https://www.aapt.org/aboutaapt/Lillian_McDermott_obit.cfm |website=aapt.org |access-date=April 28, 2021 |date=July 13, 2020}}</ref>

In the early 1970s, McDermott established the Physics Education Group (PEG) to "improve the teaching and learning of physics from kindergarten all the way through graduate school."<ref name="science">{{cite web |date=2015 |title=The science of teaching science |url=https://www.washington.edu/facultystaff/lecture/2015-university-faculty-lecture/ |access-date=April 28, 2021 |website=washington.edu}}</ref> The PEG was the first research group in the United States where students could earn a physics PhD with a research concentration in the teaching and learning of physics.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=GIREP |url=https://www.girep.org/lillian-c-mcdermott/ |access-date=2022-04-10 |language=en-GB}}</ref> McDermott led the PEG in studying student reasoning and misconceptions in physics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wheeler |first=Gerald F. |date=1991-04-01 |title=Lillian C. McDermott: Recipient of the Robert A. Millikan Lecture Award |url=https://aapt.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1119/1.16538 |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=59 |issue=4 |pages=301 |doi=10.1119/1.16538 |bibcode=1991AmJPh..59..301W |issn=0002-9505|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This work resulted in the development of the ''Tutorials in Introductory Physics'',<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=PhysPort Methods and Materials: Tutorials in Introductory Physics |url=https://www.physport.org/methods/method.cfm?G=Tutorials_in_Introductory_Physics |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=PhysPort}}</ref> as well as a curriculum for future teachers titled ''Physics by Inquiry''.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=PhysPort Methods and Materials: Physics by Inquiry |url=https://www.physport.org/methods/method.cfm?G=PBI |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=PhysPort}}</ref>

== Awards and recognitions ==
She was recognized "for her many significant contributions to the field research in physics education, especially in the area of conceptual difficulties and her role in the development of educational outreach programs at the University of Washington" with an election to the [[American Physical Society]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Washington |website=aps.org |access-date=April 28, 2021}}</ref>

She also received the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]] (AAPT) Robert A. Millikan Lecture Award in the same year.<ref name="x">{{cite web |title=Lillian C. McDermott (1931-2020) |url=https://www.um.edu.mt/__data/assets/pdf_file/0019/445033/Memorial_LillianMcDermottmm.pdf |website=um.edu.mt |access-date=April 28, 2021}}</ref> In 2021, this award was renamed the Lillian McDermott Medal in her honor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=September 2021 eNNOUNCER|url=https://www.aapt.org/Publications/responsive_September2021.cfm#Lil|access-date=2021-09-01|website=www.aapt.org|language=en}}</ref> In 2014, she was the recipient of UW's University Faculty Lecture Award, one of the highest honors at the institution.<ref>{{cite web |title=2014 Awards of Excellence recipients announced |url=https://www.washington.edu/news/2014/04/17/2014-awards-of-excellence-recipients-announced/ |website=washington.edu |access-date=April 28, 2021 |date=April 17, 2014}}</ref>
